novelty.justification: The claim predicts that “Introducing a concise linguistic label … causally improves an LLM's ability to reason about that regularity on non-linguistic/structural tasks, more than an information-matched but unlabeled exposure,” with the advantage growing with compositional depth; its novelty route is thus a new LLM-specific phenomenon and mechanism linking lexicalization, reusable compression, and structural reasoning. Searches using “LLM coined labels concept reasoning,” “naming lexicalization label advantage language models,” “nonce word definition abstract reasoning,” and “linguistic relativity LLM non-linguistic tasks” identified WinoDict (Mickus et al., 2022), which tests in-context acquisition of definition-supplied novel words, and Linguistic Overhypotheses in Category Learning (2020), which formalizes the human label-advantage effect, but neither isolates named versus information-matched unnamed concepts in LLM compositional reasoning. Moving from those works to the claim is a substantive multi-step adaptation and operationalization, especially in predicting a depth-dependent naming advantage, but it is a natural extension of established label-effect and novel-word-learning research rather than a wholly new core paradigm.
